title: Add NVTX ranges, counters, and microbench harness for runtime profiling and perf dashboards
author: Evan Lee
description: This PR instruments the serving runtime to improve visibility for kernel selection, scheduling, KV cache behavior, and continuous batching. Motivation: recurring performance regressions and a lack of fine-grained GPU timeline visibility made root-cause analysis slow during recent perf investigations (ENG-4123). Changes introduced: NVTX ranges around critical stages (model load, forward kernel execution, attention/kv cache ops, batch coalescing/schedule decisions), lightweight atomic counters for per-stage microsecond timers and op counts, a small user-facing microbenchmark harness (microbench/) to exercise batching/scheduling permutations, and scripts to export aggregated metrics to our perf dashboard. Goals: enable flamegraph-like GPU traces for common failure modes, quantify scheduling-induced tail latency, and provide reproducible microbench workloads for regression testing. Design notes: NVTX ranges are optional and gated behind a runtime flag (--nvtx-profiling) to avoid overhead in production; counters are implemented as lock-free atomics with sampling support; microbench produces a summarized CSV compatible with our grafana ingestion script. Backwards compatibility: no API changes to user-facing inference endpoints; flags are no-op when tooling is not built. Testing: unit tests for counter correctness, integration test that validates NVTX range emission using nvtx mock mode, and end-to-end microbench runs in CI. Expected perf impact: when enabled, overhead measured ~0.5-1.2% for steady-state throughput in local GPU profiling runs; benefits observed during root-cause analysis outweigh the overhead. Usage: see microbench/README.md for runbook and dashboard ingestion steps. Related work: expands on earlier lightweight tracing in perf-canary and ties into the perf dashboards in observability-pack.
